monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by reduced average HR, increased Z1/Z2 time, and slightly slower avg pace — while maintaining consistent VO2 max and efficiency.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 rose from 55% to 83% this month, while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 1%, indicating a purposeful aerobic base-building emphasis.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.2 more km across 1 session before month-end to match last month’s distance — e.g., add a 200 m walk-run cooldown to your next run.

insights.title: Efficiency dip aligns with slower pacing and lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.39 this month, coinciding with avg pace slowing by +26 sec/km and avg HR dropping 7 bpm — consistent with intentional low-intensity volume over intensity.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold and anaerobic work this month
insights.body: Z4 and Z5 combined account for only 1% of total HR time this month (vs 19% last month), with zero Z5 effort — suggesting minimal lactate threshold or VO2 max stimulus in May.

insights.title: Cadence improved despite slower pace and longer strides on faster efforts
insights.body: Avg cadence rose from 142 to 145 spm; notably, the 7:45/km effort on 5/16 achieved 145 spm with stride length jumping to 94.35 cm and ground contact dropping to 286 ms — showing neuromuscular responsiveness when pushing pace.

insights.title: Consistent VO2 max despite reduced intensity suggests adequate recovery
insights.body: VO2 max remains stable at 37.0 across all recent runs — including 5 consecutive runs in 5 days (5/12–5/22) — indicating effective recovery management and no accumulated fatigue.

recommendations.action: Perform one 4 km Zone 3 run (HR 145–152 bpm) at ~428 sec/km (7:08 min/km) pace — matching your best pace from April — to re-stimulate lactate threshold adaptation.
recommendations.reason: Z3 time dropped from 26% to 16% and Z4+Z5 vanished; reintroducing one threshold session will maintain aerobic power without compromising base.

recommendations.action: Add 30 seconds of cadence-focused drills (e.g., high-knee skips at 170+ spm) before your next two easy runs to reinforce neuromuscular efficiency gains observed at 145–150 spm.
recommendations.reason: Cadence improved +3 spm this month and correlates with lower ground contact time (308–316 ms) and stable vertical oscillation — drills will help embed this gain.

recommendations.action: Extend your longest run this month from 9.5 km to 10.5 km at Z2 HR (≤142 bpm) with target efficiency ≥13.5.
recommendations.reason: Longest run increased from 6.2 km (Apr) to 9.5 km (May), but aerobic efficiency dipped — adding 1 km at same HR zone will build stamina while testing efficiency retention.

weekly_focus.description: Blend foundational Zone 2 endurance with targeted Zone 3 stimulus to preserve VO2 max and lactate threshold adaptations while continuing base development.
suggested_sessions: 10.5 km Zone 2 long run (HR ≤142 bpm, efficiency ≥13.5)
3 km Zone 1 active recovery + cadence drills
